result:
The rain doesn't fall here anymore. Instead, the sky exhales this slow, deliberate mist that clings to everything like regret. I watch it from my window at 3:17 a.m., the only time the city feels honest. Everyone else is pretending to sleep while their devices keep their hearts racing in the dark.

I've been thinking about how we've outsourced our wonder. We used to look at the stars and feel small in a majestic way. Now we look at our phones and feel small in the worst way possible, like we're the only ones not living correctly. The algorithm knows what makes us ache and feeds it back to us in 15-second increments until our souls develop calluses.

Yesterday I found an old notebook from when I was twenty-two. The handwriting looked like it belonged to someone braver. She wrote about wanting to live inside music, about kissing people whose names she would forget, about believing time was a generous friend. I wanted to reach back through the pages and warn her, but what would I say? "Don't worry, you'll survive it all and still not know what to do with the survival"?

The mist is turning into something almost like snow now. Not real snow, of course. Nothing real happens here anymore. Just these careful, curated versions of things that feel like the real thing from a distance. I think that's what we're all doing, really. Performing believable versions of being alive.

Sometimes I miss the person I was before I understood how beautiful it is to be unfinished. Before I learned that wisdom is mostly just scar tissue with better vocabulary.

(Word count: 248)
